description: Batch the mixed-peel "rest" subset eigendecomposition instead of the current per-matrix cuSOLVER syevd loop. brief-53 idle-map measured shapes 6/7 carry 9-17 percent idle dominated by torch.linalg.eigh per-matrix syevd launch latency on the peel "rest" matrices (shape 6: ~7.8ms of sub-5us gaps across ~250 rest matrices). Route the rest subset through a single batched dense eigensolver (the existing fused mega_eigh / mega_eigh_med batched path, or one batched cuSOLVER call) so the ~250 tiny launches collapse into one, reclaiming the launch-latency idle. Targets shapes 6/7 (and any peel path with a per-matrix eigh tail). Pure torch routing change.

t1: route mixed-peel rest (263 n=512 matrices) through ONE cluster-megakernel eigh launch + orth/eigen gate + per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback. Fallback=70/263 (repeated 42/42 orth=0.96, nearrank 15/42, rankdef 7/43 -- FP16 cluster reduction leaves eigenvectors non-orthonormal). geomean 31302 vs parent 30937 (+1.2%): cluster kernel 60ms replaced cuSOLVER rest but 70-matrix fallback (5ms each) added it back.

t2: cluster-rest + NS x2 FP32 orthonormalization + Rayleigh eigenvalues + eigr gate 185*n*eps (< harness 200). Fallback 70->0. BUT profiled: cluster kernel = 53.5ms for 263 n=512 matrices; parent cuSOLVER-syevd rest was only 38ms busy (+7.75ms exposed launch idle ~46ms wall). Cluster is SLOWER: shape6 harness 144.6ms vs parent 126.2ms (+14.5%). geomean 31244 vs 30928 parent. The cluster megakernel (built for reduced low-rank k=608/768 blocks) is NOT competitive with cuSOLVER on full-rank n=512; trading 7.75ms launch idle for +15.5ms compute.

t3 WIN: force cluster C=3 for rest-batch. n=512 tridiag parallelizes better across 3 CTAs (51.9ms) than C=2 (60.4ms). PROFILED shape6: parent 4492 kernels/2289 cuSOLVER-syevd(53.8ms)/idle 12.5ms -> trial3 1711 kernels/0 cuSOLVER-syevd/cluster 1 launch 45.1ms/idle 7.2ms. Launch-latency sub5us idle 7.75ms->2.97ms. Shape6 126.2->111.1ms (-12.0%), geomean 30928->30634 (-0.95%). 0 rest fallback (NS x2 orthonorm + eigr gate 185*n*eps). 39/39 valid, stream absent.

HEAD=593cda28b3fc5864d70e2782f6485aeaa4bf5bf9 (t3), geomean ~30625us (3 runs 30634/30656/30613, stable) vs parent 30928 = -0.98%. Shape6 (mixed512) 126.2->111.0ms = -12.0%. 39/39 valid, 0 rest fallback, stream absent (grep 0).

WHAT WORKED (t3, the keeper): route _eigh_mixed_peel's rest subset (~263 heterogeneous n=512 matrices: spectrum/rankdef/nearrank/repeated/band/rowscale that no fast path caught) through ONE batched cluster-megakernel eigh launch (mega_eigh_clust_split, C=3) + FP32 Newton-Schulz x2 orthonormalization + Rayleigh eigenvalues + eigr gate 185*n*eps (< harness 200) + per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback. PROFILED shape6: parent 4492 kernels / 2289 cuSOLVER-syevd (53.8ms) / 12.5ms idle (7.75ms sub-5us launch latency) -> t3 1711 kernels / 0 cuSOLVER-syevd / 1 cluster launch (45ms) / 7.2ms idle (2.97ms sub-5us). The ~250 per-matrix syevd launches collapsed into one. Robust: 5 reseeds all PASS harness check, 0 fallback (worst rest eigr ~167*n*eps, gate 185, harness 200).

THREE KEY MEASUREMENTS that shaped it: (1) The FP16-packed cluster reduction leaves eigenvectors non-orthonormal -- repeated eigenvalues go to orth 0.96, ALL 42 fell back (t1 fallback 70/263). FP32 NS x2 orthonormalization (pure TF32 GEMM, ~1ms, environment.md's Q-through-FP32-orthonorm recipe) drives orth to 7e-6, fallback 70->0. CholeskyQR2 gives same orth but costs 11ms vs NS 1ms -- NS chosen. (2) EACH per-matrix cuSOLVER fallback costs ~5ms wall (n=512 syevd launch latency), so ANY fallback erases the win: NS x1 leaves 2 fallbacks = +25ms. (3) Cluster C matters hugely at n=512: C=3 51.9ms vs C=2 60.4ms (t2, regressed +14.5%) vs C=4 65.5ms -- the tridiagonalization parallelizes better across 3 CTAs. t2 (C=2, cuSOLVER-eq compute) LOST; t3 (C=3) won.

OPEN DIRECTIONS (concrete, unexplored):
(1) SHAPE 7 (mixed1024 b60, 17.3% idle -- the HIGHER-idle target, still untouched): it does NOT go through _eigh_mixed_peel (n=512-only) -- it falls to _eigh_twolevel's whole-batch torch.linalg.eigh (line 1417, 2-level frac 0.083 < 0.5). 60 matrices at n=1024, all per-matrix syevd. n=1024 EXCEEDS the cluster kmax 836 so the cluster kernel can't solve it directly. LEVER: matrix-sign D&C split each n=1024 into two ~512-wide blocks then cluster-solve the blocks (like _eigh_sign_dc_large does for n=2048 shape5) -- a different technique (overlaps sign-DC briefs 43/47), so I left it for a fresh brief. Shape 7 has dense(25)/psd(5) subsets that are low-rank-capturable like shape6's peel.
(2) CLUSTER KERNEL FLOOR: it is 51.9ms for the 263-rest = the dominant cost. Bisection-iter tuning barely helps (45->35 saves 0.6ms, 30 breaks). A faster tensor-core batched tridiagonalization (kernel surgery, out of a pure-torch brief) would push shape6 further.
(3) REST-CLASS PEELING: rankdef/nearrank (eff_rank 384, 85 matrices) and rowscale (rank 209, 28) are low-rank-capturable -- but _eigh_lowrank_safe on them MEASURED SLOWER than cuSOLVER (38-45ms vs 28-30ms) because the k=384 reduced-mega solve is the same slow kernel. Not a win as-is.
(4) The remaining 2.97ms sub-5us idle on shape6 is now in the OTHER peel subsets (dense/psd low-rank internal launches + routing glue) -- separate territory.

Recommend keeping t3 as parent and spawning a shape-7 sign-DC-split brief.
